$schema_note: Phase B output — theme taxonomy. Original plan (expand the enum) NOT NEEDED — the existing primary_intent enum is already well-populated. The real issue is cluster table staleness.

key_finding.headline: Existing intent taxonomy is sufficient — clusters are STALE not under-themed

evidence.diagnosis: cluster table reflects an OLD regen run (probably pre-TS-port). Once Phase D fires regen, theme count jumps ~15x without any code change.

taxonomy_decision: KEEP existing primary_intent enum as-is. 11 values is already a good spread. No new intents proposed.

minor_refinements.issue: 'development' (3) and 'feature' (488) overlap — 'development' is a generic catch-all that should be remapped to the more specific value during extraction.
minor_refinements.fix: In intelligence extraction prompt, remove 'development' as an option. Force the model to choose a specific work_category. Backfill 3 existing memories from 'development' → 'feature' or appropriate value.

minor_refinements.issue: 'ux_improvement' (1) is a one-off; 'design' (8) is barely populated. Either consolidate or leave alone.
minor_refinements.fix: Leave alone. Single-memory edge cases don't hurt clustering since HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 filters them out.

minor_refinements.issue: 1,056 memories have empty clustering_hints={} — they get NO theme assignment, even though they have project_name.
minor_refinements.fix: Backfill via Gemini intelligence extraction (existing pipeline). NOT a clustering fix per se, but it will unlock ~30% more theme assignments. Owned by intelligence extractor, not regenerateClusters.

minor_refinements.issue: Theme query uses `clustering_hints->>'primary_intent' IS NOT NULL` — but doesn't check work_category. work_category is more granular ('development', 'documentation', 'testing') and could be a SECONDARY theme dimension if user wants finer subdivision.
minor_refinements.fix: OPTIONAL — add work_category as a fallback dimension when primary_intent unavailable. Defer until after Phase D ships and we see the actual baseline.

what_phase_b_does_NOT_change: The intent enum stays the same
The theme query logic stays the same (GROUP BY project_name + primary_intent, HAVING >= 2)
The depth=0 / parent_id=project structure stays the same
The label format ('{project} — {intent.replace(_, ' ')}') stays the same
what_phase_d_will_do_for_themes: Just running the existing regen function with the alias-normalized project names will produce ~30+ theme clusters automatically

Phase A's pūrmemo merger means themes like 'pūrmemo — bug fix' (currently 452) gain memories that were previously under 'Pūrmemo — bug fix' (would have been a separate theme but disappeared because Pūrmemo only had 15 memories total, threshold-filtered)

Cognitive Orchestrator merger means 'cognitive-orchestrator — bug_fix' (~22), 'feature' (~16), 'testing' (~15), 'documentation' (~14) themes ALL surface — currently 0 themes for COS MCP because the regen never re-ran
next_steps: Phase C — orphan rescue (1,278 memories with no project_name)
Phase D — translate Phase A spec into SQL migration; baseline theme generation comes free as a side effect
